notice.title: The boats leave at 5:30 on the festival morning
notice.body: Arriving on a random afternoon will not find the procession. That leaves Front Beach at 5:30 and ends at this hall. The solar date of the 16th of the 8th lunar month moves.

body: The catalogue says the hall was built under Minh Mạng, 1820–1840, and worships the whale as Nam Hải, with Thiên Y A Na and other sea spirits. The ranked complex includes the communal house, the whale hall, and Miếu Bà. The relic list prints 104 Hoàng Hoa Thám for both Đình Thắng Tam and Linh Sơn Cổ Tự.

Outside festival days the visit is the buildings. The photograph is the whale skeleton in the hall, not the roof from the street. A licensed frame of the full facade was not the one kept. Tuoi Tre’s 2026 report followed the boats from Front Beach along the shore toward Hòn Bà, then a palanquin inland on Quang Trung, Trương Công Định, and Hoàng Hoa Thám, ending at this hall.

The rite falls on the 16th of the 8th lunar month. The 2026 public days were 26 and 27 September. Offerings, the sac-thần rite, the whale offering, hát bội, and a classical opera were in the hall on both days. A fee is not printed. Check on arrival.
